content:
Jamila Ortiz: Hey @people-ops — quick/urgent Q: our regular daycare canceled for the next 3 weeks. Is there an emergency childcare top-up or advance option we can use? Also curious if I can convert some upcoming PTO to cover hours or if there's a short-term stipend. I'm full-time. Thanks!
Nisha Patel: Sorry to hear that, Jamila. Yes — we have an Emergency Childcare Assistance (ECA) program. Two common paths: 1) monthly top-up reimbursement (up to $500/mo depending on eligibility) — submit receipts; 2) one-time Emergency Advance (repayable via payroll over 3 months) — manager approval required. Which sounds closest to what you need? :pray:
Jamila Ortiz: Top-up sounds good. Do I need manager pre-approval for that or just receipts? How fast does payment get processed if I submit receipts for last week?
Nisha Patel: Top-ups generally need receipts + people-ops approval (no pre-approval required unless >$500). Advances need manager sign-off. Payments hit the next payroll cycle if you submit by end of day Monday; otherwise it'll be the following cycle. Attach receipts, provider name, and dates on the form.
Marco Li: FYI from payroll: advances will be labeled ‘Employee Loan - ECA’ and repaid across the next 3 pay runs. Reimbursements are non-taxable if the vendor qualifies as a childcare provider — if total reimbursements exceed $600/yr we also need a W-9 on file for the vendor.
Jamila Ortiz: The provider is a small local co-op (not an LLC). If manager sign-off is needed for anything, can @Tommy approve here?
Tommy Nguyen: I approve Jamila for ECA top-up coverage up to $400/month while the daycare is closed. Please proceed with the form/receipts.
peopleops-bot: Form received: Jamila Ortiz — Emergency Childcare Request submitted at 12:04pm. Ticket #ECA-2026-1187. People Ops will review within 2 business days. :white_check_mark:
Nisha Patel: Thanks @Tommy. Jamila — once you attach receipts + provider contact we’ll process. If you want backup care vendors, check: `https://resources/redwood/backup-care` (discounts available).
Jamila Ortiz: Awesome, thank you. One more quick Q: does this policy apply to contractors? My cousin is contracting for a team and asked. Short answer?
Nisha Patel: Short answer: contractors are not eligible for ECA reimbursements. They get access to the backup-care vendor portal/discounts but not company reimbursements or advances. Contractors can invoice clients directly for coverage if arranged.
Jamila Ortiz: Got it — thanks everyone, I’ll upload receipts now.
